<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="סיון_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918872_theRebbe_254" batchId="meluket-_D7_A1_D7_99_D7_95_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918872_theRebbe_254__p006">
  <section v="15">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that at the Giving of the Torah, a new level of self-nullification called "to say" was granted, surpassing the prior self-nullification of "we will do and we will hear."</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">8)</t>
    <t s="1">And this is [the meaning of] "And G-d spoke all these words, saying,"</t>
    <t s="2">And it is explained in Chassidus,</t>
    <t s="3">that at the Giving of the Torah, the power was given that a person's study of Torah should be in the manner of "to say,"</t>
    <t s="4">to repeat the matters that the Holy One, blessed be He, says.</t>
    <t s="5">"My tongue shall answer Your word."</t>
    <t s="6">For seemingly,</t>
    <t s="7">behold, even before the Giving of the Torah, Israel preceded "we will do" to "we will hear,"</t>
    <t s="8">for the precedence of "we will do" to "we will hear" is the self-nullification of the one who possesses will,</t>
    <t s="9">and what is the innovation in the self-nullification of "to say" that was renewed at the Giving of the Torah, relative to the self-nullification of "we will do and we will hear"?</t>
    <t s="10">And the explanation of this is,</t>
    <t s="11">that the self-nullification of the precedence of "we will do" to "we will hear" has an advantage.</t>
    <t s="12">For the precedence of "we will do" to "we will hear" is the acceptance of the yoke of the kingdom,</t>
    <t s="13">and through the people accepting the yoke of His kingdom, He becomes King.</t>
    <t s="14">[And this is analogous to the self-nullification of the chariot,</t>
    <t s="15">that through the self-nullification of the chariot to the rider, thereby</t>
    <t s="16">it carries and elevates the rider.]</t>
    <t s="17">But the self-nullification of "to say" that was renewed at the Giving of the Torah is self-nullification to the ultimate degree.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="16">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that at the Giving of the Torah, the power was given for the fulfillment of commandments to be in ultimate self-nullification, where the command itself compels the person to be as commanded.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And likewise is it regarding the fulfillment of the commandments,</t>
    <t s="1">that at the Giving of the Torah, the power was given that a person's fulfillment of the commandments should be in ultimate self-nullification,</t>
    <t s="2">meaning that his fulfillment of the commandments should be</t>
    <t s="3">(not because he accepted upon himself the yoke of the kingdom of heaven and the yoke of the commandments,</t>
    <t s="4">but rather)</t>
    <t s="5">because the command of the Holy One, blessed be He, decrees upon him to be according to the command.</t>
    <t s="6">And as explained in Likkutei Torah</t>
    <t s="7">regarding the Ten Commandments that were said at the Giving of the Torah</t>
    <t s="8">[and likewise is it regarding all the commands in the Torah]</t>
    <t s="9">that they were said in the language of a command and also in the future tense,</t>
    <t s="10">for the speech itself decrees upon the person and the world</t>
    <t s="11">(and compels them)</t>
    <t s="12">to be so.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="17">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the two advantages of the self-nullification in fulfilling commandments through the command's compulsion over the self-nullification of accepting the yoke.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it may be said that the advantage of the self-nullification of fulfilling commandments in this manner, relative to the self-nullification of accepting the yoke,</t>
    <t s="1">is in two matters.</t>
    <t s="2">Because the self-nullification of accepting the yoke is through his having accepted upon himself to be a servant of the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He.</t>
    <t s="3">And beyond this,</t>
    <t s="4">that the self-nullification of a servant to his master</t>
    <t s="5">[even when he is born a servant]</t>
    <t s="6">is connected to his own existence,</t>
    <t s="7">for his essence is that he is a servant of the master,</t>
    <t s="8">but the self-nullification in the aforementioned manner is</t>
    <t s="9">(not from the aspect of the person's essence,</t>
    <t s="10">but rather)</t>
    <t s="11">that it is impossible for there to be an existence in the world that is contrary to the command of the Holy One, blessed be He.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
